title: Protocol to purify recombinant inflammatory caspases and assess their catalytic activity in vitro
protocol: Transform E. coli with the pET28a plasmid encoding caspase-4 (strain: Rosetta (DE3) pLysS).
Thaw a frozen aliquot of chemically competent cells on ice.
Add 1 μL of plasmid to the competent cells and gently flick the tube to mix.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Heat-shock bacteria for 7 min at 42°C using a temperature-controlled water bath or heat block.
Incubate the heat-shocked mixture on ice for 5 min.
Add 1 mL of SOC media to cells.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C while shaking at 250 rpm in a shaking incubator.
Plate 100 μL of bacteria on LB agar plates containing 25 μg/mL chloramphenicol and 25 μg/mL kanamycin using sterile plating beads.
Incubate for 18–24 hours at 37°C.
Pick a single colony off the plate using a sterile pipette tip.
Inoculate 10 mL of 2×YT media containing 25 μg/mL chloramphenicol and 25 μg/mL kanamycin in a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Grow pre-culture for 18–24 hours at 30°C while shaking at 250 rpm.
Inoculate the expression culture by adding 5 mL of the pre-culture to 500 mL of 2×YT media in a 2 L baffled flask.
Grow culture at 37°C while shaking at 250 rpm, regularly checking optical density of the culture at 600 nm (OD600).
Once the culture reaches an OD600 of 0.6–0.8, remove flask from shaking incubator and place on ice for 15 minutes.
While culture cools, turn down temperature of shaking incubator to 18°C.
Add IPTG to a final concentration of 0.25 mM (250 μL of 500 mM stock for 500 mL culture).
Place the culture flask back in the incubator and allow expression to proceed for 18–24 h at 18°C while shaking at 250 rpm.
Harvest bacteria by transferring cultures into large centrifuge buckets and centrifuging for 15 min at 5,000 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cell pellets in 50 mL of 1× PBS.
Collect the suspension in a single 50 mL tube.
Spin down again for 10 min at 5,000 × g.
Discard the supernatants.
Freeze down the pellets in the bottom of the tube at −20°C.
Resuspend bacterial pellet in 50 mL protein lysis buffer (∼1 mL of lysis buffer per 10 mL of expression culture).
Lysate cells by sonication (100% intensity, 2 s pulses on/off, 5 min) on ice.
Spin down intact cells and debris by ultracentrifugation (20,000 × g, 45 min, 4°C).
Filter clarified lysates through a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Transfer 0.5 mL of Ni-NTA agarose beads into a 15 mL Poly-prep gravity flow column.
Equilibrate beads with 5 mL of protein lysis buffer.
Stepwise add the clarified lysate to the column until entire volume has passed through the beads.
Discard the flowthrough.
Wash beads with 10 mL of protein wash buffer.
Label ten 15 mL tubes for collection of individual elution fractions and place on ice.
Elute bound proteins from the beads using sequential addition of 1 mL protein elution buffers with increasing imidazole concentrations (40–250 mM).
Collect each eluate fraction in individual, pre-labeled tubes and store on ice or in the fridge.
Take 40 μL of each fraction and add 10 μL of 5× SDS loading buffer.
Heat samples for 10 min at 65°C.
Assemble Mini-Protean gel running chamber.
Load 5 μL of PageRuler prestained protein ladder into the first well of the gel.
Load 20 μL of each sample into residual wells of the gel.
Run gel at a constant voltage of 180 V for 45 min to 1 hour.
Ensure the lowest band of the prestained protein ladder has reached the bottom third of the gel but not run out.
Stain gel using Coomassie to visualize proteins.
Place gel in a small plastic tray containing 25 mL of InstantBlue Coomassie protein stain.
Incubate for at least 15 min at 20°C–25°C while shaking gently.
Pool fractions containing the pure protein of interest.
Concentrate pooled eluates using an Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter unit with a 10 kDa size cutoff.
Perform buffer exchange into protein storage buffer using PD-10 desalting columns.
Place PD-10 column in holder for gravity flow protocol provided by manufacturer.
Equilibrate columns five times with 5 mL of protein storage buffer.
Discard flowthrough after each equilibration step.
Add protein solution to column.
Discard flowthrough.
If volume after ultrafiltration is below 2.5 mL, add appropriate amount of protein storage buffer to column so total volume added in this step is 2.5 mL.
Elute protein by adding 3.5 mL of protein storage buffer to the column.
Collect flowthrough in this step as eluate.
Determine protein concentration in the eluate by measuring absorbance at 280 nm using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Switch on thermocycler instrument and pre-warm to 37°C.
Add 10 mM DTT to an appropriate amount of caspase assay buffer immediately before each assay.
Thaw one aliquot of caspase-4 and pro-IL-1β on ice from the -80°C freezer.
Keep protein solutions and buffers on ice during preparation.
Set a PCR cycler to a constant temperature of 37°C.
Dilute substrate to 100 nM in caspase assay buffer.
Prepare at least 250 μL of diluted substrate for each assay.
In the first tube of an appropriately labeled 12-tube PCR strip, dilute caspase-4 to 45 μM in caspase assay buffer in a total volume of 60 μL.
Add 30 μL of caspase assay buffer to residual 11 tubes in the same PCR strip.
Perform ten 2-fold serial dilutions in the PCR strip (mix 30 μL of buffer with 30 μL of protein solution from previous tube).
Use a fresh pipette tip for each step of the serial dilution.
Add 20 μL of diluted pro-IL-1β (100 nM) to each tube of a second PCR strip.
Using a multichannel pipette, transfer 20 μL of each caspase-4 dilution to the tubes containing pro-IL-1β.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Place PCR strip into pre-warmed thermocycler and incubate at 37°C for exactly 30 min.
Set a timer to ensure proceeding of the reaction for exactly 30 min.
While reactions are incubating, prepare another PCR strip by adding an appropriate amount of 5× SDS loading buffer into each tube.
Reuse one PCR strip filled with 5× SDS loading buffer for all assays.
Store PCR strip with residual buffer at -20°C after use.
Place PCR strip in pre-warmed thermocycler for a few minutes to thaw when performing more assays another time.
Add 15 μL of 5× SDS loading dye into each tube with a multichannel pipette to stop reactions.
Set thermocycler to 65°C for 10 min to denature proteins.
Separate proteins by SDS-PAGE.
Assemble Mini-Protean gel running chamber.
Load 5 μL of PageRuler prestained protein ladder into the first well of the gel.
Load 5 μL of each sample into residual wells of the gel.
Run gel at a constant voltage of 130 V for approximately 1.5 hours.
Transfer proteins onto PVDF membrane using a wet transfer protocol in a Mini Trans-Blot cell.
Cut PVDF membrane to the appropriate size and wet it with 100% methanol for 30 seconds.
Assemble transfer sandwich in the following order: foam pad, two layers of filter paper, SDS-PAGE gel, methanol-soaked PVDF membrane, two layers of filter paper, and a foam pad.
Remove air bubbles between the layers using a roller.
Place the sandwich in the wet transfer apparatus.
Fill the wet transfer chamber with transfer buffer.
Run transfer for 1 hour at a constant voltage of 110 V.
Place the membrane in a small plastic tray and block the membrane by incubating in PBST + 5% milk for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C while gently shaking.
Rinse the membrane three times with PBST.
Incubate membrane in 10 mL of primary antibody against pro-IL-1β diluted 1:1000 in PBST + 5% BSA for 18–24 hours at 4°C while gently shaking.
Remove primary antibody solution and wash the membrane three to five times with PBST, incubating for 5 minutes per wash while gently shaking at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate membrane in 15 mL of HRP-conjugated secondary antibody diluted 1:5000 in PBST + 5% milk for 1 h at 20°C–25°C while gently shaking.
Remove secondary antibody solution and wash membrane 3–5 times with PBST.
Incubate membrane for 5 min per wash while gently shaking at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare HRP substrate solution by mixing equal volumes of the two components provided.
Add HRP substrate solution to the membrane (around 1 mL needed for a membrane the size of a regular mini gel; 8.5 cm x 6.5 cm).
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 1–5 min.
Acquire image using a ChemiDoc MP imaging system (BioRad).
Export images from internal hard drive of ChemiDoc system in a .tif format.
Open ImageJ image processing software.
Upload image in ImageJ by dragging and dropping them into ImageJ window.
Select rectangle tool and create a rectangular region of interest (ROI) around band of interest (uncleaved substrate) in the first lane (no caspase control lane).
Ensure ROI is adequately sized to fit all bands of interest.
Save first ROI position using command ‘1’.
Move rectangular ROI to the next lane and save second ROI position using command ‘2’.
Repeat for all lanes until all bands of interest are surrounded by rectangular ROIs.
Once the last ROI is in place, press ‘3’ to generate mean intensity plots for each ROI in a new window.
For each peak, generate a new ROI covering its entire area using the polygon or freehand tool.
Measure area of each individual ROI by pressing ‘M’.
Plot area values in dependency of the log of the respective caspase concentration in GraphPad prism.
Perform a nonlinear regression using the function ‘log(agonist) vs. response (three parameters)’ to obtain EC50 values.
Calculate catalytic efficiency of the reaction by using the equation provided.
